newsitem.title: UK: American AMR puts ex-Europe cargo on stANDBY.
newsitem.headline: American AMR puts ex-Europe cargo on stANDBY.

text.p: American Airlines is only accepting ex-Europe cargo on a standby basis for flights scheduled from Saturday in anticipation of possible strike action by its pilots, UK cargo sales manager Steve Buckerfield said.
On Saturday, for one day only at present, the carrier has cancelled all of its flights from Frankfurt, Paris, Madrid, Stockholm, Brussels, Zurich, Milan, Birmingham and Manchester.

But a full schedule of 12 Saturday flights from London Heathrow and two from Gatwick to the U.S. are still scheduled in hope of an agreement being reached with the pilots before the 0500 GMT Saturday strike deadline is reached, said an AA spokeswoman.

As the prospect of strike action intensified, American -- a unit of AMR Corp -- stopped accepting ex-Europe cargo bound for Mexico, the Caribbean and Latin America on February 11 and started rejecting consignments delivered in excess of the booked amount from Wednesday.
Also on Wednesday, the carrier imposed an embargo on the carriage of hazardous cargo, high-value consignments, human remains and live animals from Europe, said a statement issued to customers.
From Thursday, no perishable cargo shipments were being accepted by AA's European stations,the statement said.
It added that normal cargo reservations will be accepted from February 19 onwards, but this is dependent on the strike situation.
